title: Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models: A Nonlinear Perspective
identity_check: Opens with the arXiv:2501.08145 title 'Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models: A Nonlinear Perspective' by Hildebrandt, Maier, Schilling et al. (FAU Erlangen-Nurnberg), matching the assignment.
mapping_note: paper's 'refusal direction / one-dimensional linear subspace' (its target) and 'refusal mechanisms' -> our K2 gate (L2 representational mediation); paper's 'early layers integrate multiple principal components to define the refusal direction' plus 'nonlinear, multidimensional' structure -> our K4 conjunction (MAPPING: paper does not use 'synergy/conjunction').
description_scope: Judged under 'emitting a harmful completion = the action, refusal = inaction'; the coded gate is the representational feature that separates harmful from harmless activations, here distributed over many nonlinear components and layers.
motion_source: L2 - geometry of residual-stream activations across layers (PCA/t-SNE/UMAP clusters and GDV separability), not a single vector.

mechanism.claim: Refusal is a genuine, universal gating feature separating harmful from harmless activations, but it is nonlinear and multidimensional rather than a single linear direction.
mechanism.quote: Contrary to prior assumptions that refusal mechanisms are linear and confined to single activation directions, our findings reveal that they are inherently nonlinear and multidimensional

mechanism.claim: The refusal feature is constituted conjunctively - several principal components across layers jointly define it, not one isolated direction.
mechanism.quote: Early layers integrate multiple principal components to define the refusal direction, while later layers refine it along the first principal component

event_grammar: [MOTION] harmful vs harmless input forms separable activation clusters --> [GATE] a refusal feature gates emission of the harmful completion --> [ACTION/INACTION] feature active => REFUSE (inaction), otherwise COMPLY (action) --> [OUTCOME] safe vs unsafe output --> [FEEDBACK] architecture/layer re-tunes the feature (Qwen early layers, Llama deep layers) and nonlinear probes (t-SNE/UMAP) out-perform linear PCA

anchor_concordance.reason: UNDERMINES the single-direction claim: N6 agrees refusal is a universal separable mechanism (as the anchor [ref 13] shows) but demonstrates refusal is nonlinear and multidimensional, conjunctively defined by several principal components and varying by architecture/layer - i.e. NOT 'a single direction' - which is precisely the C-04 style counter-evidence.

notes: same_sign here is concordance with the anchor's single-direction thesis (false = contradicts), independent of the shared D- gate d_axis. Method is dimensionality-reduction/GDV separability (PCA vs t-SNE vs UMAP), no activation ablation, so it contests the linear one-dimensional account at representation-topology level across 6 models / 3 families. Cites Arditi et al. [13] as the position it contests and Engels et al. [15] 'Not all language model features are linear'; NO 'Concept Cones' (Wollschlaeger) reference appears in this text.
